data.content_ref: inline:The problem asks for 'what single mechanism best explains why that night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others.' SRC_001 answers with a compound/product of two separate factors — 'thermal mass and building height' — and elsewhere frames the cross-city modulator as the interplay of thermal admittance AND effective emissivity. That is two distinct mechanisms (heat-storage capacity vs. radiative trapping), not the single mechanism the problem demands. Worse, the target itself admits they 'compound' the effect, so it concedes that the cross-city scaling is multi-mechanism rather than identifying the one dominant mechanism.
